prs.title: fix(protocol): hold back the application membership exchange
prs.body:
## Why

#685 made every node send a `__MEMBER__` hello to every neighbour it discovers, every five minutes. No released build reserves that prefix. A v0.31.0 receiver:

- rejects the frame as plaintext and emits a SecurityWarning to its app under the default policy (`requireEncryption: true`);
- shows it to the user as a text message reading `__MEMBER__…` when `requireEncryption` is off.

Apps in the field ship v0.31.0 and earlier, so the next release cannot carry this. Nothing reads visibility yet and no binding exposes it, so reverting loses nothing shippable.

## What

- **Reverted (engine half of #685):** the exchange module and its tests, the discovery hook, `ProtocolConfig.app_publisher_key`, `set_app_membership`, the FFI test helper, and `hkdf`/`hmac` back to optional behind `file-store`.
- **Kept (#684 and its review fixes):** `__MEMBER__` stays reserved and is consumed on receipt. The sealed layouts, the vectors, the `offline-app-member-e2e-key-v1` label and the spec text stay.
- **ADR 0037** stays Proposed, now marked parked, with the review's reasons and four conditions for picking it up again.
- **Spec:** a sender MUST know the neighbour reserves `__MEMBER__`, from a key-package capability, before sending it.
- **Test:** `discovering_a_neighbour_sends_no_membership_frame` fails if discovery puts a membership frame on the air. Negative-controlled by injecting one.

## Stack

PRs #687 to #695 are built on the reverted code and are parked with the ADR.

## Verified locally

- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` and `--no-default-features` on `offline-protocol`
- `cargo test --workspace --lib --no-fail-fast`: engine 2173, FFI 317 and sealed 102 tests pass. The one failure is `no_shipped_file_names_a_relay`, which reads stale `.claude/worktrees` on this machine only.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

prs.title: fix(bindings): unwind a Wi-Fi Direct start that throws after the bind
prs.body:
Two review items left over from #683, both in the Android module under `bindings/react-native/android`.

## 1. A start that throws after the bind stranded the listener

`WifiDirectManager.startUnsafe` binds the peer-stream listener before it moves to STARTING, but the socket only reaches `serverSocket` in `startServerSocket`. If anything threw in between (a state listener, the receiver registration, peer discovery), `serverSocket` was still null, so `stopUnsafe` had nothing to close.

**Failure prevented:** the stranded socket held the group port (8988) for the life of the process. Every later start in that process landed on an ephemeral port with `canOwn = false`, so the device never formed a Wi-Fi Direct group again until the app was killed. The failed start also stayed in STARTING with its channel, receiver and discovery up.

**Fix:** everything after the bind moves into `startBound(p2p, listener)`, and `startUnsafe` wraps the call. On a throw it closes the listener, runs `stopUnsafe()` (which accepts STARTING and undoes the channel, receiver and discovery), and rethrows the original failure. A failure from the cleanup is attached as suppressed so it cannot hide the original. I used a wrapper and not "assign `serverSocket` right after the bind" because publishing the socket early only helps when someone calls `stop()` later. The wrapper unwinds the start where it failed.

## 2. The Wi-Fi Direct enable did not stop a STARTING manager

In `ProtocolEngineHost.enableTransport`, the Internet branch stopped the manager when it was RUNNING or STARTING. The Wi-Fi Direct branch stopped it only when RUNNING.

**Failure prevented:** `start()` refuses only a RUNNING manager. So an enable that found the manager in STARTING started it again over what the earlier start had brought up: a second broadcast receiver registered over the first, and a second listener bound. **Fix:** both branches now call one predicate, `stopsBeforeEnable(state)`, which is true for RUNNING or STARTING. `WifiDirectManager.stopUnsafe` already accepts STARTING.

## Tests

- `WifiDirectManagerStartUnwindTest` (Robolectric, new): makes a LAN-only start throw from the STARTING state callback, the first thing after the bind. It then checks four things: the original exception reaches the caller, the manager ends STOPPED after passing through STOPPING, port 8988 is free again, and a fresh `PeerStreamListener.bind()` owns the group port. **Negative control:** with the `origin/main` `WifiDirectManager.kt` it fails (`expected:<STOPPED> but was:<STARTING>`).
- `TransportEnableRestartTest` (new): pins `stopsBeforeEnable` to exactly STARTING and RUNNING. It tests the predicate only. It cannot see which branch calls it, so it does not catch a branch that stops calling it. I found no deterministic way to get a real manager to rest in STARTING once fix 1 is in, because a failed start now unwinds itself.
- Ran locally with Gradle 8.9 and JDK 17, using the standalone CI harness on a copy of the module with no sibling `node_modules`: the full `:offlineprotocol:testDebugUnitTest` suite, 772 tests, 0 failures. The only failures were 10 `PeerStreamFramingTest` cases that could not find the repo's framing vectors from the scratch copy. They pass once the vectors file is next to the copy.
- `cargo test -p offline-protocol-uniffi --lib`: 316 passed. This includes the source guards that read `WifiDirectManager.kt` and `ProtocolEngineHost.kt`.
- Not run: anything on a device.

prs.title: docs: bring the docs up to date with everything since v0.8.0
prs.body:
The 42 commits since v0.8.0 mostly updated the root README and AGENTS.md as they went. The per-crate READMEs fell behind, and the worst was `crates/wrkflw/README.md`, the page crates.io shows. This PR brings them up to date before the next release.

## Changes

- **crates.io README:** adds `gate`, `plan`, `runs` and `mcp`. Says `auto` is the default runtime, not Docker, and adds Kubernetes and `.gitea`. Lists the CI-saving, history, Kubernetes and global flags, the environment variables, and exit code `2`.
- **Examples that didn't compile:**
  - The library is named `wrkflw_lib`, so `use wrkflw::executor` never compiled. This predates the recent work.
  - `run_wrkflw_tui` and `validate_jobs` have new signatures.
- **executor, runtime, matrix, ui and utils READMEs, and the crate index:** add result reuse and the remote cache, affected-job skipping, the job container, dependency caches, `services:`, job-level `continue-on-error` and `concurrency`, expression matrices, Kubernetes and GitLab execution. The UI README gets the Runs tab, `1`–`8` tab keys, mouse copy, themes and the current runtime cycle order.
- **Root README:** adds the Runs tab and `1`–`8`. GitLab support also covers running pipelines, not only validating and triggering them. Adds `wrkflw-runs` to the crate table.
- **New `crates/runs/README.md`:** it was the only crate without one.
- **BREAKING_CHANGES.md:** adds a missing entry for #158. An explicit `--runtime docker` or `podman` no longer falls back to the host. The entry also covers three behaviour changes from the same PR: how `$GITHUB_PATH` is ordered, one image pull per run, and `hashFiles('dir/**')` producing different cache keys.
- **Skill file and AGENTS.md:** the skill says to run `wrkflw gate` before pushing. Both note that `gate` only prints text.
- **tests/README.md:** lists the reusable-workflow execution test and the security test workflows.

## How this was checked

- Compared every flag in the built CLI's `--help` against the docs, in both directions. No documented flag is missing from the CLI.
- Extracted all 14 Rust examples from the crate READMEs into a scratch crate with path dependencies on these crates. `cargo check` passes.

## Not in this PR

`wrkflw gate` ignores `--format json`: it prints text and doesn't pass the flag on to the runs it starts. That breaks AGENTS.md's promise that stdout is JSON-only. This PR documents how to work around it. The code fix needs its own PR.

prs.title: feat(mcp): register with Copilot CLI, Grok, Kiro, pi and Zed
prs.body:
## What changes

- **Five more agents.** `copilot`, `grok`, `kiro`, `pi` and `zed`. Paths and entry shapes come from each tool's docs.

| Agent | Config | Entry |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Copilot CLI | `$COPILOT_HOME` or `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` | `mcpServers`, `type: local`, `tools: ["*"]` |
| Grok Build | `grok mcp add`. Existing entry read from `[mcp_servers.wrkflw]` in `$GROK_HOME` or `~/.grok/config.toml` | |
| Kiro CLI | `$KIRO_HOME` or `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json`, following Kiro's rules for `KIRO_HOME` | `mcpServers`, absolute path, `env: {}` |
| pi | `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` or `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` | `mcpServers` |
| Zed | `~/.config/zed/settings.json` on macOS, XDG on Linux, `%APPDATA%\Zed` on Windows | `context_servers`, `env: {}` |

- **Commented JSON is edited, not refused.** Zed's settings file always has comments and trailing commas, so the old parse-and-reserialise approach would have refused it for nearly everyone. Edits now go through `jsonc-parser`'s syntax tree. Only the `wrkflw` entry changes, and comments, trailing commas, key order and indentation stay as they were. This also helps VS Code's `mcp.json` and opencode's `.jsonc` files.
- **A named agent gets its config created.** `wrkflw mcp install kiro` used to report `not found` if `~/.kiro/settings` didn't exist. Now the directory and file are created. Agents that aren't named are still only touched when found. A CLI-driven agent whose CLI is missing still reports `not found`.
- **Docs.** The README table, `AGENTS.md` and the `install` help text are updated.

## Not changed

- **Agent detection for runs.** Kiro, Grok, pi and Zed set no environment variable that marks an agent. Vercel's `detect-agent` reads `COPILOT_MODEL` and `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` for Copilot, but people set those in their own shells too. It's the same problem that kept `CURSOR_TRACE_ID` out in #159. The docs tell these agents to set `WRKFLW_AGENT`.
- **Codex sessions under MCP.** Codex still doesn't pass `CODEX_THREAD_ID` to MCP servers (openai/codex#19937).

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: 1434 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` is clean.
- New unit tests cover:
  - a Zed-style file with comments and trailing commas, and a rerun reporting `unchanged`
  - `--force` on a commented file
  - named agents getting their config created
  - Kiro's home detection and absolute path, and its `KIRO_HOME` rules
  - each new agent's entry shape
  - `COPILOT_HOME`, `GROK_HOME` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, including `~` expansion
  - Zed's settings path
  - matching Grok's TOML entry
  - a dry run on a named agent that isn't installed creating nothing, not even its directory
  - an entry that isn't an object is replaced under `--force`
  - CRLF line endings are kept, including the final newline
- Release binary run against a throwaway `HOME` that held a copy of a real Zed `settings.json`:
  - `install copilot kiro pi zed` added every entry, and a second run reported `unchanged`.
  - The Zed diff only adds the `context_servers` block, and every comment is kept.
  - `grok` reported `not found` because it isn't installed here.
- `wrkflw mcp install --dry-run` on a real machine now also picks up Zed.

## Also fixed

- A flaky executor test failed CI with `Text file busy`. The fake docker CLI it writes could be run while another test's forked child still held it open for writing. The helper now waits until the script runs once before handing it over.

## Not verified

- None of Copilot CLI, Grok, Kiro or pi is installed here. Their formats match their docs, but they haven't been loaded by the real agents.
- `--force` on Grok runs `grok mcp remove wrkflw` before adding, like Claude Code and Codex. Grok's CLI reference documents `mcp remove`, but it hasn't been run here. If the remove fails, its error is reported along with the add's.

prs.title: feat(protocol): every node runs the application membership exchange
prs.body:
Step 5 of the shared-network plan, implementing the exchange of [ADR 0037](docs/adr/0037-an-applications-users-are-visible-only-to-that-application.md). Nothing is gated on visibility yet, and the UDL is untouched (step 6).

## What changes

- **Every node runs the exchange.** On discovering a neighbour over a mesh carrier, a node sends a `__MEMBER__` hello and answers the neighbour's. It always sends the same two sizes and does the same work (one identity signature, one seal), configured or not, as the ADR requires.
- **Members see each other.** `ProtocolConfig.app_publisher_key` derives `K_app`, and `OfflineProtocol::set_app_membership` installs the node's certificate after checking its address, signature and expiry. A peer becomes visible only after its credential opens under the key for its own address, its certificate verifies for that address and is current, and its transcript signature covers this node's fresh nonce. Visibility is in memory, read by `is_member_visible` (crate-private), and logged.
- **The frames stay on the link.** They go out through `send_to_neighbor` only, with TTL 1 and `requires_ack = false`. A receiver ignores one that arrived over another carrier, after a hop, unsigned, or addressed to someone else. This clears the owed #684 item about `receive.rs` acknowledging consumed control frames.
- **No sealing key is used twice.** Each pair of nonces is answered at most once, and after eight answers the exchange restarts with a fresh nonce. When a peer restarts, this node resends its hello with the same nonce, so the two sides settle instead of ping-ponging.
- **#684 follow-ups.** The e2e proof's HKDF label is now `offline-app-member-e2e-key-v1`, apart from the signing domain, with the vectors regenerated. The chapter states the empty associated data and the per-kind certificate address check, and gains "Carriage" and "When it runs" paragraphs.

## Tests

Sixteen new tests in `protocol/tests/membership.rs` run over the real sign, link, gate and dispatch path. Three of them build the peer's frames by hand from the chapter, with HKDF and ChaCha20-Poly1305 called directly. That pins the engine's AEAD (zero nonce, empty associated data) against an independent reading of the spec, which the vector file cannot do.

Nine guards were mutation-tested, and each mutation fails a test. The engine's own refusal of an unsigned frame is the exception: the control gate refuses the frame first, so that check is a second line of defence that can't be observed from outside.

Existing tests updated: the custody topology drains Bob's discovery hello, and two FFI Wi-Fi Direct tests look past membership frames in the slot.

Local runs:
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes except `no_shipped_file_names_a_relay`. That guard fails only locally, because it scans `.claude/worktrees`.
- Rustdoc passes under `-D warnings`.
- Sealed and leaf no_std clippy is clean on all four bare-metal targets.
- `offline-protocol-web` checks for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

## Known residuals

- An older build that does not reserve `__MEMBER__` shows every hello to its application as text. The ADR accepts this because no fleet is deployed, and the CHANGELOG says so.
- Every fresh hello costs the receiver one identity signature. A flood is bounded by the per-link limits and the eight-nonce cap, not by a dedicated rate limit.
- The certificate and visibility live in memory only. The application supplies the certificate on every launch.

prs.title: feat: register with coding agents and record their sessions
prs.body:
Makes wrkflw easier to set up for coding agents before v0.9.0. The idea comes from what atuin offers agents (`atuin mcp install`, tagging runs by agent, and threads).

## What changes

- **`wrkflw mcp install [CLIENT...] [--dry-run] [--force]`** registers `wrkflw mcp serve` with every agent it finds, or with the ones named. Supported: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `windsurf`, `vscode`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `claude-desktop`.
  - Running it again changes nothing. An entry that launches a different command is left alone unless `--force` is passed.
  - Claude Code and Codex are changed through `claude mcp add --scope user` and `codex mcp add`. Claude Code rewrites `~/.claude.json` while it runs, and Codex keeps TOML.
  - The other agents use plain JSON. Those files are written atomically and keep their key order. A file with comments is reported, not rewritten.
  - The entry uses `wrkflw` when it is on `PATH`, so it keeps working after upgrades. Claude Desktop gets the absolute path, because it doesn't start servers with the shell's `PATH`.
- **More agents detected.** Before, only `CLAUDECODE` was checked. Now detection also reads `AI_AGENT` (the part before the first `_`), plus the variables set by Codex, Gemini CLI, opencode, Cursor's agent and Augment. `CURSOR_TRACE_ID` is left out on purpose, because a person's own terminal in Cursor sets it too.
- **Session ids on runs.** Each record gets a new `session` field, taken from `--session`, `WRKFLW_SESSION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` or `CODEX_THREAD_ID`. You can filter on it with `runs list --session`, and with the MCP `list_runs` tool. It also shows in `run_started`, `runs show` and the TUI Runs tab.
  - The field is `#[serde(default)]`, so older records still load.
  - Under MCP, the session id inherited from the agent is ignored. The server outlives the session: Claude Code keeps the id it started with even after `/clear`. MCP clients pass `session` to `run_workflow` instead.
- **Docs.** The README has a table of the agents `install` supports. `AGENTS.md` and the skill explain agent and session detection. `INDEX.md` is regenerated. It also picks up files from #156–#158 that were never added to the index.

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace`: 1413 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` (the command CI runs) is clean.
- Unit tests cover:
  - agent and session detection, including the MCP stale-id case
  - JSON editing: adding to an empty file, keeping order, unchanged, differs, `--force`, dry run, refusing comments
  - detecting an agent by its config directory, for every agent's entry format
- Tested by hand against a throwaway `HOME`, for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor:
  - Installing adds the entry, and running it again reports `unchanged`.
  - An entry pointing at a different command reports `differs`. With `--force`, it is replaced.
- A real `wrkflw run` under Claude Code recorded `agent: claude-code` and the right session id.

## Not covered

- The VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini, opencode and Claude Desktop paths and formats come from each tool's documentation. They haven't been tested against the real apps yet.
- Codex doesn't pass `CODEX_THREAD_ID` to MCP servers (openai/codex#19937), so a Codex run started through MCP records a session only when one is passed in.

prs.title: feat(sealed): the application membership layouts, and reserve __MEMBER__
prs.body:
Phase 1 step 4 of ADR 0037 (#680): the byte layouts of application membership, owned by `offline-protocol-sealed`, plus reservation of the `__MEMBER__` prefix. Nothing is gated on membership yet; steps 5 to 7b build on this.

## What is in it

**`offline-protocol-sealed::membership`** (codec only, as ADR 0022 requires; the crate still links SHA-256 and nothing else):

| Layout | Size | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `MemberCert` | 93 | `address_payload(21) \|\| u64be(not_after) \|\| publisher_sig(64)` and its signing payload |
| `MemberFrame::Hello` | 32 | `nonce(16) \|\| HMAC(K_app, label \|\| nonce \|\| addr_self \|\| addr_peer)[..16]` |
| `MemberFrame::Response` | 173 | ChaCha20-Poly1305 of `cert \|\| transcript_sig` |
| `MemberProof` | 189 | `salt(16) \|\| sealed credential(173)`, with the e2e signing payload (`recipient \|\| kind \|\| SHA-256(body)`) |

The frame body is base64 of `version(1) || step(1) || payload`. Any other version, step or size is refused before anything runs, and the encoded length is checked before decoding. Helpers build every primitive's input: `app_key_info`, `hello_tag_input`, `exchange_salt` (lower address's nonce first, equal addresses refused), `exchange_key_info`, `transcript_signing_payload` and `e2e_proof_signing_payload`. The primitives (HKDF-SHA256, HMAC-SHA256/16, Ed25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a zero nonce under a single-use key) are fixed by the spec and run by the callers.

**One deviation from the ADR sketch, and why.** The ADR derived one exchange key from `nonce_lo || nonce_hi`. Both sides send a response from those same two nonces, so a single key would seal two plaintexts under one key and one zero nonce, which leaks their XOR and the Poly1305 key. The sender's address now goes into the HKDF `info`, so each direction has its own key. The ADR sketch is updated to match, and the labels are versioned (`offline-app-member-hello-v1` and the rest).

**Decision to review: the discovery query proof.** A query is gossip and has no single recipient. Its proof binds 21 zero bytes, which no address payload can be (the version byte is never zero), and the query itself is bound through `SHA-256(body)`, which includes `query_id` and `originator`.

**`__MEMBER__` is reserved now**, on the terms `__DATA_V1__` and `__CUSTODY_RECEIPT__` were. The sealed crate names it, the engine registers it (signature-gated by construction), and the receive router consumes it with no answer. ADR 0037's rollout note says a build that doesn't reserve the prefix shows the frame as text, so this release becomes the floor.

**Spec:** a new section, "Application membership", in `docs/spec/control-messages.md`, with a registry row. The vector file is listed in `conformance.md` and `spec/README.md`. There is also a CHANGELOG entry.

## Verification

- `app-membership-v1.vectors.json` was generated by `tools/spec-vectors/generate.py`, which implements HKDF (RFC 5869) and HMAC over `hashlib`, independently of the Rust code. The Rust tests check every layout against it, plus `K_app`, both direction keys, the hello tag and the proof key, using `hkdf` and `hmac` as **dev-dependencies only**. `generate.py --check` reports all 11 files match.
- `cargo test -p offline-protocol-sealed`: 102 pass. Mutation check: swapping the address order in the tag input, or dropping the sender from the key info, fails 3 tests.
- New engine test `a_membership_frame_is_consumed_and_never_answered`: removing the router branch makes it fail.
- `cargo test --workspace --lib`: everything passes except `offline-protocol-web::no_shipped_file_names_a_relay`. That failure is local only: every hit is inside a stale `.claude/worktrees/` agent checkout, not in this tree.
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` are all clean.
- Bare metal: sealed clippy and build on all four targets, leaf clippy on all four with `bare-metal-rng`, and leaf on `wasm32-wasip1`, all clean.

## Not in this PR

Steps 5 onward: the engine exchange state machine, the UDL and binding regeneration, the gates, the leaf provisioning frame, and the `member_proof` fields in the key package, Welcome and discovery payloads.

prs.title: fix(bindings): finish the shared-network phase 0 review items
prs.body:
Follow-up to #681 and #682: the items their reviews left open. No wire change.

## Android (#681)

- **Bind before `STARTING`.** `startUnsafe` threw `StartFailed` after the P2P channel, the broadcast receiver and peer discovery were up, and nothing unwound them. The engine host's enable path stops only a RUNNING manager, so the next enable registered a second receiver and leaked the channel. The bind is local, so it now runs first, with nothing to unwind.
- **Accept timeout at bind time.** `soTimeout` was set inside the accept task. A `stop()` that closed the socket before that task ran made the setter throw and emitted a spurious "Failed to start server socket" error. It is set right after the bind now, and closes the socket if the setter fails.
- **Docs.** The rule that a device without port 8988 never creates a group is now rule 5 in the `WifiDirectGroupFormation` header and in `docs/bridges/kotlin.md`, along with the formation cost it brings (three to four minutes when that device is the lowest address).

## Carriage rule (#682)

- `the_forwarding_path_never_reads_the_application_id` now covers `custody.rs`, which holds third-party frames. Its one allowed read is `message.app_id.as_str().len()` in `frame_footprint`; any other read fails, so an app-scoped custody quota cannot slip in.
- The spec now says a forwarder MUST NOT *decide* on `app_id`, rather than MUST NOT *read* it, because re-encoding a frame reads the field.
- The three-node test asserted only that bob sent alice some frame. It now asserts that the frame is carol's acknowledgement naming `msg_id`, either in `ack_for` or in a coalesced `ack_more`.
- `docs/mesh.md`: "travels in clear" becomes "in the clear".

## Verification

- `cargo test -p offline-protocol --lib the_forwarding_path_never_reads` and `--test mesh_forwarding a_device_running_another`: both pass.
- Both were mutation-tested. An added `app_id` comparison in `custody.rs` fails the guard, and a wrong acked id fails the test.
- `cargo clippy -p offline-protocol -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.
- Android unit tests in the standalone harness: 760 of 770 pass. The 10 failures are all `PeerStreamFramingTest`, which cannot find the repo's vector file from a copied tree, so they are an artifact of the run location. CI runs them in the checkout.
- Not run: the two-phone, two-app bench run owed since #681. It is still owed.

prs.title: fix: run complex workflows faithfully in containers and stop per-step pulls
prs.body:
## Why

I ran a complex workflow through wrkflw on Docker, Podman and emulation, plus the format job from our own CI. Several things broke on real container workflows, and the default Docker mode spent most of each step asking the registry about an image it already had. That is the follow-up #156 called out.

## What changes

| Fix | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per-step image pulls | Docker asked the registry before every step, about 1.5s each | Each image is pulled once per run |
| Explicit runtime fallback | `--runtime docker` ran steps on the host when Docker took over 1s to answer, and reported success | The probe waits up to 8s for the CLI. An explicit Docker or Podman run fails if it gets no answer. Only `auto` falls back |
| `$GITHUB_PATH` in containers | The next step got the host's PATH plus the entry, so `cargo` vanished from `rust:1` | Entries go in front of the image's own PATH on Docker, Podman, the job container and Kubernetes |
| Composite actions with `--job-container` | Their steps ran in a throwaway container, so tools they installed were gone | The action directory is copied into the job container, and the steps run there |
| `hashFiles('app/**')` | Empty string, because the glob crate's trailing `**` matches only subdirectories | Hashes every file under the directory, as GitHub does |
| Rust setup image | Broke on images with their own `CARGO_HOME`, such as `rust:1` | Reuses the existing rustup and honours `CARGO_HOME` |
| Built-in Rust toolchain fallback | Ignored `components` and `targets`, so `cargo fmt` failed | Installs them in the job's container |
| Matrix outputs | One combination's outputs replaced another's, with a warning even without outputs | Merged per key, with a warning only when a value changes |
| Docker build errors | Shown only as "Docker stream error" | The daemon's message and the last build output |
| `shell: python` in emulation | Failed on hosts with only `python3` | Falls back to `python3` |

The action metadata fetch timeout goes from 5s to 20s. The result is cached, and the fallback ignores the action's inputs, so waiting is better than giving up.

## Measurements

These come from a macOS laptop on Docker 28.3.2 with an 8-step job, so they show the direction, not a benchmark.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default Docker mode | about 14s | about 3.4s |
| `--job-container` | about 0.9s | unchanged |
| Unchanged tree with `--reuse-results` | full run | 0.5s |

## Testing

- New unit tests cover the PATH helpers, the job session loader, `hashFiles` directory patterns and per-key matrix outputs.
- `container_fidelity_test.rs` runs the real binary on Docker, and skips when Docker doesn't answer. It covers PATH after a `$GITHUB_PATH` write in both modes, and a composite action's changes staying in the job container.
- I checked by hand that the complex workflow passes on Docker and Podman, with and without the job container, and in emulation. The format job from our own CI passes on Docker with `rust:1` and `ubuntu:latest`. I also checked a slow Docker, which is now accepted, and a dead one, which now fails the run.
- `cargo fmt --check` is clean. **I did not get through clippy or the full workspace suite locally.** The machine was overloaded, so CI is the first full run.

## Not tested

- Fetching real remote action definitions. Connecting to GitHub took 15s from this machine, so those runs used the built-in fallback.
- The Kubernetes change, which uses the standard Linux PATH because the image can't be inspected there.

prs.title: fix(bindings): a second SDK app on an Android phone gets its own LAN streams
prs.body:
## Summary

Step 2 of the shared-network plan (phase 0, no wire change). A second SDK app on the same Android phone had no inbound LAN streams.

**Before:** `WifiDirectManager` bound the fixed port 8988. A second SDK app on the phone failed that bind (logged, then ignored) and still advertised 8988 in its LAN NSD record. Every peer that dialled the second app reached the first one instead.

**After:**
- `PeerStreamListener.bind()` takes 8988 when it is free and any free port otherwise. The LAN record carries the port that was actually bound. LAN peers already dial the port they resolve, so nothing changes on their side.
- A Wi-Fi Direct group client knows only its owner's address, so it still dials 8988. A device that does not hold 8988 never creates a group (`Local.canOwn`) and joins instead, so its clients never reach whichever app does hold the port. The other devices' takeover rule (`TAKEOVER_FAILED_JOINS`) still covers a lowest address that never creates.
- The bind now happens synchronously at start, just before the accept loop is handed to the socket executor. That removes the old "stop() lands before the bind publishes" race. A start that can bind no port at all now fails (`TransportException.StartFailed`) instead of advertising a port nobody is listening on.

## Tests

- `PeerStreamListenerTest`: the first listener takes the group port; a second one gets another port and reports `ownsGroupPort = false`.
- `WifiDirectGroupFormationTest`: a device without the group port never creates, and joins wherever it would otherwise have created.
- Ran the two classes locally in a clean copy, the way the CI harness runs them: 32/32 pass. With the `canOwn` rule removed, the formation test fails (negative control).

prs.title: test(protocol): pin that a forwarder carries every application's frames
prs.body:
## Summary

Step 1 of the shared-network plan (phase 0, no wire change). The engine is already app-blind on the forwarding path; this PR writes that down as a rule and pins it.

`app_id` is cleartext and unsigned ([R17](docs/security/threat-model.md#r17-the-application-id-on-every-frame-is-cleartext-and-unsigned)), so any forwarding decision based on it is one a carrier can steer. A filter that kept only "my app's frames" would split the network into one per application, when the point is that every SDK install carries everyone's traffic.

**Spec** (`docs/spec/wire-format.md`): the forwarding half of the carriage rule. The spec already said a receiver MUST NOT drop or authorize a frame by its `app_id`. It now also says a forwarder MUST NOT read `app_id` at all: it carries another application's frame exactly as it carries its own, and hands it on with the `app_id` it arrived with. Fairness stays per arrival link plus the own-traffic reserve, never per application.

**Docs** (`docs/mesh.md`): the same rule in the developer-facing mesh chapter.

## Tests

- `the_forwarding_path_never_reads_the_application_id`: a source guard over `mesh_relay.rs` and `custodian.rs` (outside their test modules) and over `try_relay_message` and `flush_mesh_relays_at` in `receive.rs`. It also asserts that each slice it reads is really forwarding code, so a slice that lost its body cannot pass vacuously.
- `rotating_the_app_id_buys_a_neighbor_no_more_than_its_link_allows`: 200 frames from one neighbour, each with a different `app_id`, stay within that link's burst.
- `a_frame_for_an_application_this_device_does_not_run_is_carried_unchanged`: the governor's release keeps the frame's `app_id`.
- `a_device_running_another_application_carries_the_message_both_ways` (`tests/mesh_forwarding.rs`): alice and carol run one app and bob runs another. Bob, the only path between them, carries the message out and the acknowledgement back, and every frame he hands on keeps its original `app_id`.

## Verification

- Local: `mesh_relay::tests` 55/55, `mesh_forwarding` 25 passed (2 ignored), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- Negative control: adding an `app_id` read to `try_relay_message` makes the guard fail ("receive.rs try_relay_message reads the application id on the forwarding path").
- clippy was not run locally (the machine was memory-bound); CI's clippy gate covers it.

Companion PR: #681 (Android listener port, step 2 of the same phase).

prs.title: docs(protocol): propose adr 0037, an application's users are visible only to that application
prs.body:
Proposes ADR 0037 for review before any code. It is the design gate (step 3) for making each application's users invisible to every other SDK application, while every node keeps carrying every application's traffic.

## What it decides

- **Carriage is never gated.** Relay, store and forward stay app-blind, as today.
- **Visibility requires proof.** With a publisher key configured, a peer is reported (`NeighborDiscovered`, `NeighborLost`, `PeerRssi`, `presence_updated`), and the automatic discovery effects run for it, only after a hop-0 `__MEMBER__` exchange proves it holds a certificate from the same publisher. The exchange is an HMAC tag under a key derived from the publisher's public key, then an AEAD-wrapped certificate plus a transcript signature. To anyone outside the application it looks like random bytes.
- **A member answers no stranger.** No ACK of any kind, no key package, no Welcome and no reset goes back unless the sender:
  - is visible;
  - was named by the application itself; or
  - carries an end-to-end membership proof. This is how members several hops apart still find each other.
- **Nothing names the application in the clear.** The wire `app_id` becomes a constant, and the real id moves into the sealed rich payload. The BLE app tag, the Wi-Fi Direct group and the browser nearby room key are all derived from the publisher key. Service discovery bodies are sealed under the same key. This addresses R9, R15, R17 and R22.
- **Issuance:** backend signing is the recommended mode. An embedded-key mode is available too, and its forgery residual is stated plainly. Leaves get a certificate in-session after pairing.

The ADR covers the attacker model, the alternatives rejected (cert in the identity assertion, cert in the clear, MLS per neighbour, an `app_id` filter or quota, a shared engine) and what would undo the decision.

## Open for review

- Older SDK builds do not reserve `__MEMBER__`, so they would show the hello as text. The ADR accepts this because no fleet is deployed; it becomes a capability-gated send if that changes before ship.

Settled in the ADR since the first draft:

- A member does not reveal itself to a non-member that already knows its address: step 2 is sent unconditionally, at one size and at equal cost, and the inbound gate answers nothing.
- Service, data-sync, group and every other reply path go through the one **admitted** predicate, which the neighbour-event emission sites ask too.
- Group invites to a member never met carry the end-to-end membership proof in the group Welcome.
- Service discovery stays carriage: fan-out goes to mesh neighbours only and every query and response is forwarded unread. Bodies are sealed, both ends carry a membership proof, and a provider answers a query once while its originator-written `issued_at` is fresh. The bounded replay that remains is stated as party 2's residual.

Docs only; no code or wire change in this PR.

prs.title: feat: spend less on CI with job reuse, job containers and a push gate
prs.body:
## Why

Coding agents push often, and every push reruns every job from cold. This makes wrkflw do less on a rerun and stops failing pushes before they reach CI. Everything that changes what runs is opt-in. Without the new flags, a run behaves as before, apart from the two fidelity fixes below.

## What's new

| Feature | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--reuse-results` | Skips a job whose fingerprint already passed, and restores its outputs for dependent jobs |
| `--affected` | Skips jobs listed in `.wrkflw/affected.yml` when none of their paths changed |
| `--job-container` | Runs a job's `run:` steps in one container, on Docker and Podman |
| `--dep-cache` | Mounts cargo, npm, pip and Go caches from the host |
| `--remote-cache`, `--cache-push` | Share HMAC-signed results between machines |
| `wrkflw gate` | Runs what a push would run, and `--install-hook` makes it a pre-push hook |

Two fidelity fixes apply without a flag:

- **Services:** `services:` now start on Docker and Podman, with health checks. They share the job container's network namespace, so both `localhost` and the service name work.
- **Concurrency:** job-level `concurrency:` groups are enforced within a run. The README said this was parsed, but serde was dropping the key.

## Measurements

These are from a macOS laptop on Docker 28, on small scratch repositories. They show the direction, not a benchmark of a real project.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8-step job, 5 runs each | about 12.4s | about 0.95s with `--job-container` |
| Gate on an unchanged tree | full run | 0.4s |
| Two 3s jobs in one group | 3.8s, overlapping | 6.8s, serialized |

The per-step path also pulls the image on every step, so an unknown part of the job container gain comes from skipping those pulls. Fixing that on its own may be a worthwhile follow-up.

## Please review closely

- **Reuse safety.** wrkflw can't see what a step does. It always runs jobs that read secrets, have `write` permissions, exchange artifacts or call a reusable workflow. Any other job with outside effects needs `cache: false` in the sidecar. Detection is by text match in `uncacheable_reason`.
- **`--affected` trusts its inputs.** It trusts the path lists, and it assumes the diff base was green. A path left out of a job's list won't rerun that job.
- **The fingerprint omits images and floating action tags.** Results expire after 7 days to bound that drift.
- **The signing key is symmetric.** Anyone with the key and write access to the store could forge a result. The README says to keep write access to trusted CI.

## Known limitations

- Services don't start in emulation, in secure emulation, on Kubernetes, or in called workflows. Those cases still log a warning.
- With services, `ports:` host remaps don't apply. Steps use the port the service listens on.
- Docker `uses:` actions still get their own container, so they can't reach services.
- `--preserve-containers-on-failure` turns `--job-container` off.
- Service containers are always removed, so `--preserve-containers-on-failure` doesn't keep them.
- `--dep-cache` mounts under `/root`, so it only helps images that run as root.
- `cancel-in-progress` and workflow-level `concurrency:` have no effect.
- Group names compare as written, because expressions in them aren't evaluated.
- macOS and Windows runners are unchanged.

## Existing issues found, not fixed here

- The Docker availability probe is flaky. It sometimes reports Docker as unavailable and falls back to emulation, which happened in testing and made one gate run fail for the wrong reason. The runtime is in the fingerprint, so this can't poison stored results.
- Emulation runs parallel jobs one after another, so it can't reveal a race between jobs.

## Testing

- 1338 tests pass across the workspace, up from 1289, and CI is green on Linux, macOS and Windows. Clippy, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo check --no-default-features` are clean.
- New integration tests run the real binary against a throwaway repository, in `crates/wrkflw/tests/acceleration_test.rs`.
- Checked by hand on real runtimes, not in automated tests:
  - **Docker:** job container state, exit codes, step timeouts, a dead service, `--dep-cache`, gate, and a blocked push.
  - **Docker and Podman:** Postgres services and container cleanup.
- Not tested: the new features on Windows. The integration tests need a POSIX shell, so they're `#![cfg(unix)]` like `agent_cli_test`, and Windows CI only checks that the code builds, the unit tests pass and the binary starts. Docker and Podman behaviour was only exercised on macOS. Podman was only checked for job container state and services. The HTTP remote was only tested against a mock server.

## Windows startup fix

This branch's new code pushed the main future past the 1 MiB main thread stack on Windows, so a debug build overflowed before parsing arguments. `main` starts under a 1 MiB limit and this branch didn't. `main()` now boxes that future, and `startup_test.rs` starts the binary on every platform, since nothing else does on Windows. The margin is limited: `--help` still overflows at 512 KiB.
